note: Window agent m4900-m4801: one event restoring 43 cells of the Samarra culture's keyframe (Diyala east of Samarra and the western rim of the As Sulaymaniyah circle) that the Ubaid has held since 5100 BCE. Reviewer: note corrected (the Ubaid keyframe includes these cells; it does not subtract them).

region.text: the Samarra culture's own land: the middle Tigris around Samarra and Tell es-Sawwan and the As Sulaymaniyah circle

events.note: 4900 BCE (window start; the cells left the Samarra culture at 5100 BCE with no event): the Samarra culture, "c. 5500 - c. 4800 BCE", holds its land to its end; the Ubaid page: "In central and northern Iraq, the Ubaid culture was preceded by the Hassuna and Samarra cultures". 43 of the 249 cells of the Samarra keyframe have been the Ubaid's in the draft since 5100 BCE: 32 in the Babylonia region east of Samarra (Diyala 31, Baghdad 1; 29 of them in the Samarra circle), added by the ubaid-period_-5100 keyframe snap, and 11 on the western rim of the As Sulaymaniyah circle (Kirkuk 7, Erbil 3, Salah ad-Din 1), taken by the 5100 BCE Jazira/Assyria gain from the Halaf. The Ubaid keyframe of 5100-4801 subtracts the Samarra circle from its northern part only, but its text keeps the middle Tigris Samarran "until 4800 BCE", its note calls the Sulaymaniyah overlap "a region boundary, not a claim", and the Ubaid ledger gains the Samarra circle from the Samarra culture only in 4800 BCE. The cells return to the Samarra culture until its end, when its dissolve hands them to the Ubaid.
